hyps.why: Replacing a missing edge into the output with a 3x3 conv restores the node-2 path and the strongest op, so the gain is much larger than when replacing an existing op.
With edge 2->3 already removed, cutting the direct 0->3 edge leaves only the node-1 route to the output, so removal is far more damaging.
Without the direct 0->3 path, removing 1->3 eliminates a remaining output path and risks a near-disconnected cell.
If 0->2 is absent, removing 0->1 zeroes both intermediate nodes, leaving only edge 3 to carry information.
A residual shortcut on 0->3 helps most when the deep path through node 2 already contains a strong conv, mimicking a ResNet block.
Swapping a 3x3 conv for a parameter-free pool on the last edge discards the most useful op, so the edit hurts more than when replacing weaker ops.
Node 2 cannot reach the output when edge 2->3 is none, so adding a conv on 0->2 provides essentially no benefit.
Edge 1->2 feeds node 2, which is dead without edge 2->3, so improving it yields little gain.
Turning a missing 0->1 edge into a 3x3 conv activates node 1 and its downstream paths, a far larger gain than swapping an existing op.
When 0->1 is none, node 1 outputs zero, so putting a conv on 1->3 carries no signal and gives little benefit.
